Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Taylor Voss, CFO; Morgan Lee, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a strong quarter for Apex EV. We made significant progress in several key areas, including advancing our production ramps, strengthening supply chain resilience, expanding gross margins through cost discipline, optimizing pricing to drive volumes, and executing on our strategic priorities amid a dynamic EV market. The demand for our flagship Apex One midsize SUV continues to be strong, with its impressive 28kWh/100km efficiency and proprietary 800V architecture exceeding initial expectations, and we're working diligently to scale capacity for the new Apex Bolt pickup as well.

Before we dive deeper into the financials, let me share our strategic outlook and priorities for Q4 and into fiscal 2025. The EV landscape is evolving rapidly—global sales reached 14 million units last year according to the IEA, with penetration at 18% worldwide, though we're navigating uneven regional dynamics like softening demand in Europe, intense competition from BYD and Tesla in China, and tailwinds from the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act. At Apex EV, we're focused on execution to deliver sustainable profitability while leading in premium EVs and light trucks.

Our guiding principle is vertical integration and cost discipline, emphasizing LFP battery chemistries for affordability. We've hit 22% automotive gross margins this quarter, up 500 basis points sequentially, thanks to our Nevada Gigafactory ramp and Shanghai localization. We're guiding for 25-27% automotive gross margins by year-end 2024, excluding credits, with company-wide EBITDA margins expanding to 12-15% in FY25 as volumes grow.

First priority for Q4 is production ramp and delivery acceleration—we're targeting 125,000 vehicle deliveries, a 35% quarter-over-quarter increase and 60% year-over-year growth. That includes 85,000 units of the Apex One and 40,000 of the Apex Bolt pickup, rivaling the F-150 Lightning and Cybertruck. We've resolved early 4680 cell constraints with Panasonic adding 20GWh capacity by Q1 2025, pushing Fremont and Berlin plant utilization to 95% by December from 82% now.

For FY25, we aim for 500,000 annual deliveries, a 2.5x jump from 2024, with fleet-wide ASPs steady at $52,000 despite pricing pressures. This factors in a mix shift to higher-margin trucks at 40% of volume and the sub-$40k Apex Spark hatchback launching H1 2025 to grab mass-market share where Tesla dominates with 55% in the U.S.

Second, supply chain resilience and cost reductions—battery costs are down 18% year-over-year to $85/kWh equivalent, blending LFP from our CATL JV at 60% of packs and in-house NMC. We're targeting another 25% drop to $65/kWh by end-2025 via cell-to-pack tech and silicon-anode pilots scaling to 10% of output. We've hedged 70% of lithium and nickel at Q3 prices, shielding from the 15% cobalt spike.

CapEx is $3.2 billion this year, with $1.8 billion for Gigafactory Texas Phase 2 adding 150GWh for structural packs and $800 million for autonomy compute. Free cash flow turns positive in Q4 at $200-300 million, scaling to over $2 billion in FY25, funding 80% of growth without dilution.

Third, regional expansion—North America at 65% of FY25 revenue leverages IRA's $7,500 PTC and $45/kWh credits on U.S.-made packs for 15% U.S. EV share by 2026 from 8% today. Q4 promotions target fleets like Hertz and Uber for 20k commercial deliveries, with Mexico plant starting Q1 2025 for USMCA exports.

Europe at 20% of revenue sees Berlin output doubling to 30,000 units quarterly for EFTA compliance. The Apex Bolt EU variant with 500km WLTP range targets 12% premium share by FY25 end at €55k ASP.

China/APAC at 15% ramps Shanghai Gigafactory #2 to 50k monthly in Q4, localizing 85% BOM against tariffs on BYD's Seagull. We're gaining in the ¥150k-250k segment with Blade LFP packs offering 8% better cycle life, plus BAIC and Geely white-label vans adding $500 million revenue.

Fourth, autonomy and software—Electra Autonomy Suite v2.5 rolls OTA to 200k vehicles in Q4 for Level 3 hands-free on highways with Nvidia OrinX at 500 TOPS. Robotaxi pilots launch Austin and Shanghai H1 2025, eyeing $1 billion recurring software revenue by 2027 at 30% take rates. Energy storage deployed 2.5GWh this quarter via Powerwall rivals and Megapack contracts.

Headwinds like high interest rates on EV financing at 6.5% versus 4% for ICE and U.S. inventory gluts at 60 days persist, but our 92-day order-to-delivery beats Tesla's 45-day average, avoiding deep discounts. Competitors like Ford at 5% margins on Mach-E and GM's Ultium delays highlight our vertical edge.

Risks include lithium deficits projected by S&P Global at 20% by 2026 and regulatory shifts, but $10 billion liquidity and 3x net debt/EBITDA provide strength. Solid-state prototypes with QuantumScape target 700Wh/kg for 1,000km range in 2027.

In short, Q4 positions us for FY25 with $28 billion revenue, up 80%, 18% EBITDA margins, and a 1 million run-rate path by 2026. We're shaping the EV future.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Taylor Voss:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue was $6.7 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 22.1%, reflecting ongoing operational improvements. Operating expenses were $1.2 billion, and net income was $450 million. We maintain a healthy balance sheet with $10 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for Q4 is revenue of $7.5 to $8 billion, with gross margins at 24-25%.

Today, I'd like to unpack our gross margin performance, a cornerstone of profitability in this competitive EV space. Gross margin—revenue minus COGS over revenue—hit 22.1% consolidated, up 190 basis points sequentially from 20.2% in Q2 and 410 basis points year-over-year from 18%. That's six straight quarters of expansion, with trailing 12-month average at 20.8%. Automotive segment alone was 21.5%, excluding energy storage and software growth.

Full-year 2024 guidance holds at 23-25%, Q4 at around 24.5% with stable ASPs and supply tailwinds. This outpaces Rivian's negatives and matches Tesla's 18-20% amid cuts.

Key drivers: COGS reductions, especially batteries at 35-40% of BOM. Cell costs dropped 15% sequentially to $85/kWh via CATL LFP blades and in-house 46-series at Nevada. Gigacasting with Giga Press 2.0 at Berlin cuts machining 25%, part count from 400 to 70, assembly to under 10 hours, variable COGS to $32,500 per vehicle from $38,200.

Favorable mix: ASPs at $52,800, up 3% QoQ, with premium Apex at 38% volume (28% margins), CyberHawk pickup at 22% (26%), offsetting entry-level. Energy products added $450 million at 35% margins.

Regionally: North America 52% deliveries at 24.8% margins via IRA $7,200 per vehicle on 65% domestic content. Europe 28% at 20.3%, pressured by subsidy cuts but strong on fleets. China/APAC 20% at 17.5%, improving with localization.

Scale absorbed fixed costs—92% utilization across four gigafactories versus 75% YoY, overhead to 7.2% of revenue from 9.5%. FY deliveries on track for 450,000, Q4 at 150k run-rate.

Upside from 28% FSD subscriptions at $1,200 ARPU, 90% margins, and $180 million credits at 100%. We're targeting 70% in-house BOM by 2026, with AI supply chain cutting scrap to 1.2%, pushing margins above 25% long-term.

Pricing strategies and promotions also shaped results. We delivered 128,000 vehicles, up 22% YoY, beating guidance by 5,000. U.S. retail up 15%, Europe 28%, but ASP at $52,400, down 7% YoY and 3% sequentially—intentional, offset by volumes for $6.7 billion automotive revenue, 92% of top line.

In the U.S. (55% deliveries), IRA $7,500 credits on Apex 300, 0% APR to 72 months on Apex 300/500, $5,000 lease cash on Apex 400 lifted leases to 42%. ASP down 9% to $49,800, volumes up 25%, inventory to 42 days from 65, gaining 1.2 points share to 8.4% versus Ford.

Europe (25%), countered subsidy cuts with €500/month leases on Apex 300 plus chargers and OTA, clearing inventory, 55% leases. ASP down 6% to €48,200, deliveries up 32% versus VW.

China (15%), matched BYD with 12% cut on Apex 200 to ¥135,000, ¥10,000 trade-ins, 10-year warranties. ASP down 10% to ¥148,000, but profitable per unit with $55/kWh cells.

Margins at 21.8%, down 240 bps YoY but flat sequentially—offset by 15% 4680 savings, OTA Level 3/V2G mix shift to 35% premium at $70k+, flat COGS at $41,000 despite 22% growth. Promotions on 40% inventory, FCF $450 million.

Q4 ASP stabilizes at $52,000 as promotions ease, trucks to 20% at $85k.

Raw material costs and disruptions were headwinds—BOM 45% battery metals, 60% cell costs. Inputs up 12% YoY: nickel 18% to $18,500/tonne on Indonesian quotas, lithium 25% to $18,200/tonne on restocking, cobalt down 5% to $28,000.

This compressed margins 220 bps pre-mitigation to 22.6%; 4680 NCM811 up 14%, LFP 7%—hence 35% LFP mix from 22%. Disruptions cut output 7% or 12,500 vehicles on LG/Northvolt delays; Red Sea added 14-21 days/$4,500/FEU, ocean up 32% to $185 million; Panama aluminum delays 15,000 tonnes.

North America (62%) localized 65% lithium for IRA; Europe graphite delays 8,000 units; Asia nickel squeezes.

Mitigations: 70% 2025 nickel/lithium hedged 15% below spot, saving $220 million; 50GWh BYD Brazil LFP from Q1 2025, China exposure to 42%; Ultium Ohio 46-series 20GWh year-end.

Dry electrode pilots cut NMP 90%, cobalt 30%; Redwood recycling 12,000 tonnes black mass, 4% inputs at 40% less. Q4 costs flatten, margins to 24.5%, FY production 285,000, EBITDA $1.2 billion.

Before segments, a supply chain update—critical amid sector headwinds. We've limited impacts to 8% QoQ versus peers' 12-15%. Semiconductor lead times 28-32 weeks for ADAS/powertrain, 12% F-series SiC shortfall; lithium $18,000/tonne up 25%, nickel $21,000 up 18%; Asia 65% disruptions, CATL 4-6 weeks, Red Sea 40% freight, Long Beach 2 weeks.

Shaved 2.2GWh throughput, $150 million revenue hit at $120/kWh, COGS to 68%, turns to 4.2x.

Mitigations: '3-2-1'—3 suppliers, dual lines, in-house; semis 30% to Samsung/GlobalFoundries, Asia to 55%; Northvolt 20GWh NMC, SK On 15GWh LFP.

ApexCell JV with Redwood at 10GWh Nevada run-rate, 4680-style 5% denser/18% cheaper, 25% cathodes, PPM <50; 25GWh year-end, $1.2B capex offset $300M IRA.

Stockpiles to 90 days, 40% air freight caps 15%; AI platform 92% disruption accuracy.

Sodium-ion pilots 10% fleet 2025, no Co/Li, 3,000 cycles/160Wh/kg; cell-to-pack 65% density, 12% BOM cut; solid-state 400Wh/kg 2025.

IRA 70% U.S. $45/kWh, Berlin EU rules, Vietnam BYD routing 95% OTIF.

EBITDA 12.4% beat Tesla 9.8%, 15% procurement savings; H2 ease with Intel Ohio, lithium +20%; 80% 2025 fixed, derisking $2.5B.

Production guidance 120,000 FY24.

I'll now turn the call over to Morgan Lee to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Morgan Lee:
Thank you, Taylor. We're pleased with scaling Apex One and Bolt production. Initiatives like gigacasting, cell ramps, and AI optimization are boosting efficiency and cutting costs. Nevada Phase 1 at 10GWh, Berlin utilization rising, Shanghai localizing. We're on track for 125,000 Q4 deliveries and FY24 targets, with defect rates under industry norms and utilization hitting 95%.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star two two. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks for the update. On supply chain, how confident are you in Q4 production given lingering chip and battery issues?

Taylor Voss:
Sarah, great question. Our mitigations are robust—diversification reduced Asia exposure, ApexCell insources 25%, and stockpiles cover 90 days. We've secured 80% of 2025 at fixed prices, so Q4 guidance is firm at 125,000 units.

Operator:
Next question from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Patel:
Jordan, your FY25 500k target—any mix assumptions or risks from China competition?

Jordan Hale:
Mike, the 500k assumes 40% trucks, Spark launch, steady $52k ASP. China risks are real, but Shanghai ramp and partnerships mitigate; we're profitable there per unit.

Operator:
Our next question is from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong:
Taylor, gross margin trajectory looks strong—any color on Q4 drivers versus pricing pressures?

Taylor Voss:
Lisa, Q4 at 24.5% driven by scale, 92% utilization, cell costs to $85/kWh, and mix toward premiums. Pricing stabilizes as promotions taper.

Operator:
Next from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz:
Morgan, manufacturing-wise, how's the gigafactory ramp impacting costs?

Morgan Lee:
David, Nevada at 10GWh run-rate with 18% lower costs, gigacasting slashing parts 80%, assembly under 10 hours. On track for 25GWh year-end.

Operator:
One more from Emily Grant with Deutsche Bank.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Emily Grant:
Taylor, raw materials—lithium rebound, how's hedging holding up?

Taylor Voss:
Emily, hedges cover 70% of 2025 at 15% below spot, saving $220 million. Q4 peaks then 10-15% pullback expected, supporting margin rebound.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Update on supply chain constraints and mitigation strategies
Strategic outlook and priorities for the next quarter/year
Impact of pricing strategies and promotional activities
Impact of raw material costs and supply chain disruptions

aspect_summary.Update on supply chain constraints and m: Constraints include chip/semiconductor lead times (28-32 weeks), battery cell delays (LG/Northvolt, CATL 4-6 weeks), raw material spikes (lithium +25%, nickel +18%), Red Sea freight +32%, limiting impact to 8% QoQ vs. peers' 12-15%; mitigations via '3-2-1' diversification (3 suppliers/dual lines/in-house), 70-80% 2025 hedging at 15% below spot ($220M savings), ApexCell JV insourcing (10-25GWh), 90-day stockpiles, AI disruption prediction (92% accuracy), new suppliers (BYD Brazil, Northvolt/SK), tech (cell-to-pack, dry electrode), supporting Q4 125k deliveries confidence.
aspect_summary.Strategic outlook and priorities for the: Q4 priorities: production/delivery ramp to 125k units (+35% QoQ, +60% YoY, 85k Apex One/40k Bolt), supply chain resilience/cost reductions (battery to $65/kWh by 2025), regional expansion (NA 65% revenue via IRA/Mexico, Europe 20% Berlin double, China/APAC 15% Shanghai ramp), autonomy (Electra v2.5 OTA, robotaxi pilots H1 2025); FY25: 500k deliveries (2.5x 2024), $28B revenue (+80%), 18% EBITDA (12-15% start), steady $52k ASP, 40% truck mix, Spark hatchback launch H1, vertical integration/LFP focus for profitability.
aspect_summary.Gross margin percentage and trends: Q3 consolidated 22.1% (+190bps QoQ from 20.2%, +410bps YoY from 18%), automotive 21.5-22%; six straight quarters expansion, TTM 20.8%; drivers: cell costs -15% to $85/kWh, gigacasting (-25% machining), 92% utilization, premium mix/energy/software; Q4 24-25% (~24.5%), FY24 23-25%, YE24 auto 25-27% excl. credits, long-term >25%.
aspect_summary.Impact of pricing strategies and promoti: Intentional ASP reductions (Q3 $52,400-52,800, -7% YoY/-3% QoQ) via US 0% APR/lease cash ($5k), Europe €500/mo leases+chargers, China 12% cuts/¥10k trade-ins drove 128k deliveries (+22% YoY, beat guidance), inventory to 42 days (US), share gains (US 8.4%); volumes offset ASP drop for revenue growth/$6.7B auto, margins flat seq. at 21.8%; Q4 ASP stabilizes $52k as promotions ease/trucks rise to 20-40%.
aspect_summary.Impact of raw material costs and supply: Raw materials +12% YoY (nickel +18% to $18.5k/t, lithium +25% to $18.2k/t, cobalt -5%); disruptions (LG/Northvolt -7% output/12.5k vehicles, Red Sea +14-21 days/$4.5k FEU/+32% freight $185M, Panama Al 15k tonnes) compressed margins 220bps pre-mitigation (4680 +14%, LFP +7%, LFP mix to 35%); hedged 70% 2025 needs (15% below spot, $220M save), localization/diversification flatten Q4 costs, enable 24.5% margins.
